evidence: (a) Present under another name: no current-generation reopening/correction transition is specified. Lines 98 and 108 describe new-generation rebuilding and deterministic reconstruction, but neither is a repair operation for an erroneous closure; I do not count them as such. (b) Within the stated contract: this refutation lands. The spec explicitly limits its guarantee to workers seeing and citing classified human items, and says that it 'does not guarantee that the model correctly recognizes every answer' (line 72). Line 76 assigns semantic completion to the worker and explicitly says the daemon cannot prove that an answer satisfies the user or that a claimed build succeeded; line 104 likewise makes rule-quote meaning a 'cooperative derived-summary judgment'. Thus erroneous semantic judgments are an acknowledged consequence of the contract, not an unaddressed promise of semantic correctness. Older closed entries being omitted is also expressly specified (lines 78 and 110), with source messages and receipt state preserved. (c) Out of stated scope: the proposal reuses existing summary-worker resolution (lines 17 and 62), specifies only forward closure statuses (line 104), and excludes a dedicated resolve command and other resolution protocols (line 80). A new repair/reopening lifecycle would strengthen the inherited derived-summary contract, rather than satisfy a stated requirement of this classification and cross-chunk-visibility change. The referenced existing summary design section 5 also permits only closure of still-open items and omits older closed items, confirming this is inherited behavior rather than a new regression. (d) Immaterial: a mistaken closure can affect recovery, so its potential effect is real; this check alone does not refute the concern. However, the stated guarantees are deterministic source preservation, visibility for worker judgment, structurally valid cited transitions and correct rendering of recorded state, not correction of all mistaken semantic judgments. The finding is literally right about the absent repair operation but does not survive the explicit accepted-tradeoff check.
